options.name: init_config
options.description: All options defined here are available to all instances.

options.name: global_custom_queries
options.description:
See `custom_queries` defined below.

Global custom queries can be applied to all instances using the
`use_global_custom_queries` setting at the instance level.

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Additionally, this sets the default `service` for every log source.

options.name: instances
options.description: Every instance is scheduled independently of the others.

options.name: server
options.description: The hostname used to connect to the system.

options.name: reported_hostname
options.description:
Set the reported hostname for this instance. Overrides the default hostname resolution,
which uses the `server` value. Useful when the agent connects via localhost or 127.0.0.1
(e.g., co-located with ClickHouse in the same pod) to avoid reporting a non-unique hostname.

options.name: port
options.description:
The port used to connect to the system.
This integration uses the HTTP interface, so the default is 8123 (HTTP port).
Note: Port 9000 is for ClickHouse's native TCP protocol, which is not used by this integration.

options.name: username
options.description: The database user to authenticate as.

options.name: password
options.description: The password of `username`.

options.name: db
options.description: The database to connect to.

options.name: connect_timeout
options.description: The timeout for connecting to the `server`.

options.name: read_timeout
options.description: The timeout for reading from the `server`.

options.name: compression
options.description:
The compression algorithm to use. The default is no compression.
If br is specified, the brotli library must be installed separately.

Valid values are:
  - lz4
  - zstd
  - br
  - gzip

options.name: tls_ca_cert
options.description: The path to the CA certificate file.

options.name: tls_verify
options.description: Whether or not to connect securely using TLS. The server must also support this.

options.name: verify
options.description: Indicates if a certificate is required and if it will be validated after a connection is established.

options.name: dbm
options.description:
Enable Database Monitoring (DBM) to collect query samples, metrics, and completions.
This feature provides deep observability into query performance.

options.name: database_identifier
options.description:
Controls how the database is identified. Each unique value of this identifier will appear in DBM as a separate
billable instance.

The default value is "$server:$port:$db" which uniquely identifies a ClickHouse database by its server, port,
and database name.

This value will be used as-is for the display name of the instance but will be normalized
when applied as the `database_instance` tag. Please see https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/tagging/
for more details on Datadog tag normalization.

options.name: template
options.description:
The template string for the database identifier. Supports variable substitution using $variable syntax.
Available variables: $server, $port, $db, plus any custom tags (e.g., $env, $region).

options.name: single_endpoint_mode
options.description: Set to `true` when connecting through a single endpoint for ClickHouse Cloud.

options.name: use_legacy_queries
options.description: Enable the legacy query set for collecting metrics. Set to `false` to disable.

options.name: use_advanced_queries
options.description: Enable the advanced query set for collecting metrics. Set to `false` to disable.

options.name: query_samples
options.description: Configure collection of database samples snapshots from system.processes

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of database samples snapshots. Requires `dbm: true`.
Samples snapshots show currently executing queries and connection counts.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the samples snapshot collection interval (in seconds). Each collection involves a single query to
`system.processes` to capture currently executing queries.

options.name: payload_row_limit
options.description: Set the maximum number of active sessions to include in each samples snapshot.

options.name: query_metrics
options.description: Configure collection of query metrics

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of query metrics. Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the query metric collection interval (in seconds). Each collection involves a single query to
`system.query_log`. If a non-default value is chosen then that exact same value must be used for *every*
check instance. Running different instances with different collection intervals is not supported.

options.name: query_completions
options.description: Configure collection of query completions from system.query_log

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of query completions. Requires `dbm: true`.
These samples represent individual completed queries and appear on the DBM Query Samples page.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the query completions collection interval (in seconds).
Lower values show more recent queries but increase collection overhead.

options.name: samples_per_hour_per_query
options.description:
Set the maximum number of samples to collect per hour per unique query signature.
This rate limiting prevents excessive data collection for frequently executed queries.

options.name: collect_async_inserts
options.description: Configure collection of async insert flush events from system.asynchronous_insert_log.

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of async insert flushes. Requires `dbm: true`.
These records represent individual flush events (dbm_type="async_inserts_flush"), including flush
status, exception (if any), bytes, and row count per flush.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the flush log collection interval (in seconds). Each collection runs a single
query against system.asynchronous_insert_log.

options.name: max_samples_per_collection
options.description: Maximum number of flush records to collect in a single run (applies LIMIT in SQL).

options.name: query_errors
options.description: Configure collection of query errors from system.query_log

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of query errors. Requires `dbm: true`.
Collects ExceptionBeforeStart and ExceptionWhileProcessing events, which include
exception message, error code, and stack trace.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description: Set the query errors collection interval (in seconds).

options.name: samples_per_hour_per_query
options.description: Set the maximum number of error samples to collect per hour per unique query signature.

options.name: schema_metrics
options.description:
Configure per-table size and per-view refresh gauges derived from
`system.tables` and `system.view_refreshes`. Independent of
`collect_schemas` (which controls catalog structure collection)
so users can dashboard table sizes without enabling Schema Explorer.
Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of per-table size and per-view refresh gauges.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the schema metrics collection interval (in seconds). These
gauges change continuously, so 60s is a reasonable default.

options.name: collect_schemas
options.description:
Configure collection of ClickHouse catalog metadata (databases,
tables, views, columns) for Database Monitoring's Schema Explorer.
Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of catalog metadata. When enabled, the agent
polls `system.tables`, `system.columns`, and
`system.view_refreshes` (ClickHouse 24.3+) and emits one
`kind=clickhouse_databases` payload per cycle.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the schema collection interval (in seconds). Catalog data
changes slowly; 600s (10 min) is a reasonable default.

options.name: max_tables
options.description:
Maximum number of tables plus views to collect per cycle
across all databases.

options.name: max_columns
options.description: Maximum number of columns to collect per table/view.

options.name: max_query_duration
options.description:
Maximum duration of the schema collection queries in seconds.
Applied to each query via the `max_execution_time` ClickHouse setting.

options.name: include_databases
options.description:
A list of regex patterns to include databases. Any database whose
name matches any one of these patterns will be included. If empty,
all databases (other than those excluded) are included.

options.name: exclude_databases
options.description:
A list of regex patterns to exclude databases. Any database whose
name matches any one of these patterns will be excluded. The
ClickHouse system databases (`system`, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`,
`information_schema`) are always excluded regardless of this setting.

options.name: include_tables
options.description:
A list of regex patterns to include tables. Any table whose name
matches any one of these patterns will be included. If empty, all
tables (other than those excluded) are included.

options.name: exclude_tables
options.description:
A list of regex patterns to exclude tables. Any table whose name
matches any one of these patterns will be excluded.

options.name: parts_and_merges
options.description: Configure parts and merges monitoring

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of parts and merges monitoring. Requires `dbm: true`.
Emits per-table gauge metrics (clickhouse.table.parts.*, clickhouse.merges.*, clickhouse.mutations.*,
clickhouse.replication.*) for trend dashboards and alerting, plus a row-level event payload per
collection cycle consumed by the DBM Storage Health timeline view.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the parts and merges collection interval (in seconds). All four system tables
(parts, merges, mutations, replication_queue) are queried on each run.

options.name: max_parts_rows
options.description:
Maximum number of rows to include in the per-cycle event payload from system.parts,
ordered by active_part_count descending. With `table_metrics_include_partition_tag`
disabled (default) rows are aggregated per-table server-side, so this caps tables.
When partition tagging is enabled, rows are per-partition and this caps partitions.

options.name: max_mutations_rows
options.description:
Maximum number of rows to include in the per-cycle event payload from system.mutations,
ordered by create_time ascending. Caps payload size when many mutations are pending.

options.name: max_detached_parts_rows
options.description:
Maximum number of rows returned from system.detached_parts per cycle.
Applied as a raw SQL LIMIT; increase only if your cluster has a pathological number
of (database, table, reason) combinations in detached storage.

options.name: max_replication_queue_rows
options.description:
Maximum number of rows returned from system.replication_queue per cycle,
ordered by position ascending. Busy replicated clusters can exceed the default
during incidents; raise this if replication queue backlogs are being truncated.

options.name: table_metrics_include_partition_tag
options.description:
Add a partition tag to parts gauges (clickhouse.table.parts.*).
Disabled by default to avoid high cardinality: a table partitioned by day over two years
yields ~730 partitions and hundreds of additional metric series per table.
Enable only when per-partition alerting is explicitly needed.

options.name: table_metrics_max_tables
options.description:
Cap per-table gauge emission to the top N tables by active part count.
Guards against pathological schemas with very large numbers of tables or partitions.

options.name: stalled_merge_elapsed_threshold_seconds
options.description:
Number of seconds a merge must be running before it is counted as stalled
in the `clickhouse.merges.stalled` gauge. Raise this threshold if long-running
merges are expected in your environment (e.g. large Wide-part merges on spinning
disks) to avoid false-positive stall alerts.

options.name: stuck_replication_num_tries
options.description:
Minimum number of failed attempts (num_tries) before a replication queue entry
is counted as stuck in the `clickhouse.replication.stuck` gauge. Entries below
this threshold are still counted in `clickhouse.replication.queue.depth`.
Increase this value if transient failures routinely exceed the default before
self-healing.

options.name: collect_pending_async_inserts
options.description: Configure asynchronous insert buffer snapshot monitoring

options.name: enabled
options.description:
Enable collection of asynchronous insert buffer snapshots from system.asynchronous_inserts.
Requires `dbm: true`. Sends per-buffer records as DBM events (dbm_type="async_inserts_buffer")
including the query text, showing bytes pending, pending entry count, and scheduled
flush deadline per buffer.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description:
Set the buffer snapshot collection interval (in seconds). Each collection runs a single
query against system.asynchronous_inserts.

options.name: max_samples_per_collection
options.description:
Maximum number of buffers to collect in a single run (applies LIMIT in SQL).
Prevents overwhelming the agent with too many buffers at once.

options.name: only_custom_queries
options.description:
Set this parameter to `true` if you want to skip the integration's default metrics collection.
Only metrics specified in `custom_queries` will be collected.

options.name: use_global_custom_queries
options.description:
How `global_custom_queries` should be used for this instance. There are 3 options:

1. true - `global_custom_queries` override `custom_queries`.
2. false - `custom_queries` override `global_custom_queries`.
3. extend - `global_custom_queries` are used in addition to any `custom_queries`.

options.name: custom_queries
options.description:
Each query must have 2 fields, and can have a third optional field:

1. query - The SQL to execute. It can be a simple statement or a multi-line script.
    Use the pipe `|` if you require a multi-line script.
2. columns - The list representing each column, ordered sequentially from left to right.
    The number of columns must equal the number of columns returned in the query.
    There are 2 required pieces of data:
      1. name - The suffix to append to `<INTEGRATION>.` to form
          the full metric name. If `type` is a `tag` type, this column is considered a tag and applied
          to every metric collected by this particular query.
      2. type - The submission method (gauge, monotonic_count, etc.).
          This can also be set to the following `tag` types to tag each metric in the row with the name
          and value of the item in this column:
            1. tag - This is the default tag type
            2. tag_list - This allows multiple values to be attached to the tag name. For example: 
                ```
                query = {
                  "name": "example",
                  "query": "...",
                  "columns": [
                    {"name": "server_tag", "type": "tag_list"},
                    {"name": "foo", "type": "gauge"},
                  ]
                }
                ```
                May result in:
                ```
                gauge("foo", tags=["server_tag:us", "server_tag:primary", "server_tag:default"])
                gauge("foo", tags=["server_tag:eu"])
                gauge("foo", tags=["server_tag:eu", "server_tag:primary"])
                ```
            3. tag_not_null - This only sets tags in the metric if the value is not null
          You can use the `count` type to perform aggregation for queries that return multiple rows with
          the same or no tags.
    Columns without a name are ignored. To skip a column, enter:
    ```
      - {}
    ```
3. tags (optional) - A list of tags to apply to each metric.
4. collection_interval (optional) - The frequency at which to collect the metrics.
    If collection_interval is not set, the query will be run every check run.
    If the collection interval is less than check collection interval, the query will be run every check
    run.
    If the collection interval is greater than check collection interval, the query will NOT BE RUN
    exactly at the collection interval.
    The query will be run at the next check run after the collection interval has passed.
5. metric_prefix (optional) - The prefix to apply to each metric.

example.query: SELECT foo, COUNT(*) FROM table.events GROUP BY foo

options.name: tags
options.description:
A list of tags to attach to every metric and service check emitted by this instance.

Learn more about tagging at https://docs.datadoghq.com/tagging

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.

options.name: min_collection_interval
options.description:
This changes the collection interval of the check. For more information, see:
https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/write_agent_check/#collection-interval

options.name: empty_default_hostname
options.description:
This forces the check to send metrics with no hostname.

This is useful for cluster-level checks.

options.name: metric_patterns
options.description:
A mapping of metrics to include or exclude, with each entry being a regular expression.

Metrics defined in `exclude` will take precedence in case of overlap.

options.name: logs
options.description:
Log Section

type - required - Type of log input source (tcp / udp / file / windows_event).
port / path / channel_path - required - Set port if type is tcp or udp.
                                        Set path if type is file.
                                        Set channel_path if type is windows_event.
source  - required - Attribute that defines which integration sent the logs.
encoding - optional - For file specifies the file encoding. Default is utf-8. Other
                      possible values are utf-16-le and utf-16-be.
service - optional - The name of the service that generates the log.
                     Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.
tags - optional - Add tags to the collected logs.

Discover Datadog log collection: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/log_collection/
